prompt: [Final Product to Create] This instruction sheet and the attached full-body reference image will be used as the sole person reference to convert the person into a high-quality anime character wearing prestigious Kyudo attire while maintaining identity. Create one practical 1:1 square character sheet that is beautiful for sharing and provides a stable reference for person, clothing, body type, and basic color scheme in subsequent video generation. Stage settings are not handled in this sheet. [Person Reference] Image A = one full-body reference image. Maintain Image A's facial features, eyes, outline, nose, mouth, hairstyle, hair color, bangs, parting, body type, head-to-body ratio, shoulder width, waist position, leg length, overall proportions, and impression. Age and gender are not fixed by text but inherited from Image A. Do not perform excessive beautification, rejuvenation, making them look like a different person, facial downsizing, body type changes, or excessive leg extension. [Anime Conversion] Regardless of whether the reference is a live-action photo or an illustration, the final character should be unified into a high-quality anime style. It should not be a halfway expression but a natural anime drawing where the face, hair, body, and clothing are consistent. [Hairstyle] Maintain Image A's hairstyle, hair color, bangs, parting, and facial area. Short to shoulder-length hair should remain as is; only if long hair interferes with movements should it be naturally tied at a low neck position. Do not add buns, high ponytails, or flashy ornaments not in the reference. [Kyudo Clothing and Equipment] Arrange as prestigious Kyudo Japanese clothing. Based on a white upper garment, black to dark blue hakama, obi, and white tabi, carefully draw fabric overlaps and folds. The chest protector (mune-ate) must be consistent across front, side, and back views with continuous strap structures. Do not change its shape or position between views. **The yugake (archery glove) and wrist gear are worn only on the right hand. The left hand does not wear a yugake in any view. In the front view, hold the Japanese bow (wakyu) with the left hand and wear a brown/ocher yugake on the right. Maintain the yugake on the same right hand in all views; do not swap hands or add/remove it inconsistently. Equipment shape and color must match in all views. No purple or blue accents.** The bow is naturally held only in the front full-body view and removed in side/back views for clarity. [Sheet Composition] Align front, profile, and back full-body views of the same person/outfit at the same scale. The front view can be slightly larger, but do not diminish side/back views. Do not include face close-ups. [Color Bar] Place one thin horizontal 4-color proportional bar in the lower margin (white, dark blue, warm yugake tones, dark brown hair/bow). It should be an auxiliary element, not a thick sample. No color names, codes, or icons. [Design and Layout] Unify the design with the stage setting sheet series. Background is light gray. Place the title "KYUDO CHARACTER SHEET" at the top center with thin horizontal lines. Center the three views and place the color bar at the bottom. [Prohibitions] Face close-ups, expression variations, action poses, tiny side/back views, stage backgrounds, text other than title, thick color chips, family crests, purple/blue wrist gear, **yugake on the left hand, or changing the wearing hand between views.** [Priority] 1. Person identity 2. View consistency and utility 3. Body proportion maintenance 4. Consistent clothing and right-hand yugake 5. Natural anime conversion 6. Color scheme clarity 7. Design consistency. [Final Product to Create] Create one high-quality anime-style Kyudo dojo/stage setting sheet for background reference. It organizes the same dojo from three main directions for video use. [Input] Aspect ratio: [1:1]. [Basic Policy] Prioritize practicality. Match wood, pillars, floor, walls, ceiling, roof, target area, lighting, and time of day across all views. Fix to high-quality anime background art with clear morning-to-noon natural light and a calm atmosphere. Do not draw people. [3-View Composition] 1. Upper main view: Standard view looking from the shooting area to targets with clear depth and architecture. 2. Lower left view: Side background for sideways filming. A flat background of wooden floors, plaster walls, and pillars. No corridors or strong perspective. 3. Lower right view: Frontal background for front-facing filming. High symmetry with a central recessed plain wall surface. No windows or hanging scrolls. Distinguish from side view via the central depth. [Text Elements] No text in the stage space (signs, slogans, etc.). Use only the title "KYUDO STAGE SETTING SHEET" at the top. [Layout] Title at top center. Upper row: main view. Lower row: side and frontal backgrounds in two columns. Light gray background with minimal decoration. [Prohibitions] Architectural changes between views, side view corridors, making lower views identical, targets on side walls, people, windows, readable text, or atmospheric cuts of unknown role. [Priority] 1. Dojo consistency across views 2. Shooting range-target relationship 3. Flat side background 4. Frontal background depth 5. Clear structural difference between lower views 6. Reproducibility 7. Organized design.
